summary.intent: Finish wave-6 review of seven PRs (#1116-#1123), fixing all findings, resolving review threads, and getting every PR to a green CI state before merge.
summary.outcome: All ten review findings across six PRs were fixed and threads resolved (#1118 merged); a worker-recovery race in #1117 was fixed and mutation-verified; while re-checking CI, a real semantic merge conflict between merged #1118 and #1123 was discovered (a FUSE cache-invalidation test broken by #1123's write-plane changes) and delegated to an agent for a non-vacuous fix, with #1116/#1117 CI re-triggers still pending.

repo: The FUSE kernel-cache-invalidation test (`the_first_read_invalidates_the_kernels_data_cache_for_the_inode`, from #1118) detects staleness indirectly by diffing `projected_content(node)` before/after opening the stream, not by tracking kernel state directly — this makes it fragile to unrelated changes in projection timing.

Worker recovery (`requestPorts()`) runs at script-evaluation time rather than inside an event handler; its returned promise must be retained and chained to the triggering fetch, or the browser can terminate the worker before `clients.matchAll()`/messaging completes, silently skipping recovery.
PRs that are each individually green can still produce CI failures when merged/rebased together due to semantic (not textual) merge conflicts — confirmed here between #1118 and #1123.

code.finding: Kernel-stale-data detection compares `projected_content(node)` pre/post stream-open; #1123's changed head-version projection makes this comparison a no-op even when the kernel is genuinely stale, silently defeating the invalidation signal.
File modified in the wave-6 session (fix location for #1117 worker-restart/recovery-promise issue).

workflow: Verify a fix is load-bearing via mutation testing: revert only the fixed line and confirm the new test becomes the sole failure, then restore and confirm full pass.
When two independently-green PRs fail in combination, reproduce on `main` first to rule out flake or bad rebase before investigating the interaction.
Sequence CI re-triggers rather than firing them all at once, to avoid queueing on top of runs still resolving.
When delegating a red-test investigation to an agent, explicitly instruct it not to weaken the assertion to force green and to prove any fix is non-vacuous.

friction: #1123's fix commit showed 4 CI failures that turned out to originate from already-merged #1118's FUSE test, not from #1123's own changes — required cross-PR log investigation to isolate.
The semantic merge conflict between #1118 and #1123 wasn't caught until after #1118 was merged, since each PR passed CI independently.
